narrative:
The model predicts a 96% chance that you will leave your job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This high probability reflects patterns the system sees in your overall profile that strongly align with employees who end up departing.

Three factors stood out as the most influential in this decision. First, your total years of professional experience pushed the prediction most strongly toward leaving. With over 11 years across all roles, you sit in a small minority—only 14.7% of employees predicted to stay have this level of experience. The model sees longer overall careers as a signal that someone is more likely to move on.

Second, the fact that you have received other job offers while working here also pulled the prediction toward leaving. Employees who get external opportunities are far more likely to depart than those who do not.

Third, your relatively short time in your current role—between one and five years—further increased the likelihood of leaving. This places you with the majority of people the model expects to stay (51.2%), yet in your specific combination with high total experience it still contributed to the “will leave” direction.

Taken together, these elements suggest you may be at a career stage where external options become attractive. The organization should discuss your long-term goals and what would make you want to grow here. You may want to reflect on whether your current path still matches your ambitions. (248 words)
